source: Hersche, Camposampiero et al. (2024/2025) Towards Learning to Reason: LLMs vs neuro-symbolic on arithmetic relations (Table III, predictive vs discriminative)
finding: Direct LLM test of 'predict the missing panel first, then match to options' against 'show the options and pick'. On I-RAVEN centre (leak-free answer sets), the predictive route beat the discriminative route for both models, most of all for Llama-3 70B. In the predictive route the final match to the options is done by code (count of overlapping attribute values), not by the LLM.
numbers: I-RAVEN centre, no self-consistency, no per-attribute split: GPT-4 discriminative 56.0 and 60.0 (two rows) vs predictive 74.8; Llama-3 70B discriminative 22.8 and 22.4 vs predictive 79.0. Adding per-attribute queries: 91.4 / 83.2; plus self-consistency n=7: 93.2 / 84.8.
quote: the predictive classification can be seen as a more guided approach
limits: Not matched on tokens (prompts differ in length). The two discriminative rows differ by a setting lost in the PDF layout. Oracle text attributes, 2024 models, no context-blind options-only control run. Option matching by code removes LLM option-confusion, so part of the gain is tooling.
agent_relevance: Best direct evidence for gap 1: build the answer first, then match it to options with a deterministic step. Supports a construct-then-compare operator and an options-hidden first pass. Still needs the equal-token and options-only control run on our own items.

source: Hersche, Camposampiero et al. (2024/2025) same paper, Tables IV-VI and Appendix C (error analysis of the arithmetic rule)
finding: The arithmetic-rule weakness is mixed. Part is a rule-induction failure (the model infers a rule from the last row only). Part is range or length handling, because it collapses further as value range grows. No calculator tool was tested.
numbers: For GPT-4, 32 of 68 arithmetic errors could be explained by a rule inferred from a partial context (for example constant or progression from the last row). Arithmetic accuracy fell below 10% for both LLMs at range 1000 (GPT-4 8.4%, Llama-3 0.4%). Disentangled queries at the small range lifted GPT-4 arithmetic from 27.1% to 73.6%.
limits: No tool arm. 'Explained by' is a post-hoc fit, not a causal test. Self-consistency n=7 used in the range sweep.
agent_relevance: Do not assume a calculator alone fixes arithmetic rules. Add a step that forces use of the first two rows before reading the last row, and add executable checking. Gap 8 stays open until a with-tool run exists.

source: Camposampiero, Hersche, Wattenhofer, Sebastian, Rahimi (2025) Can large reasoning models do analogical reasoning under perceptual uncertainty? (Table 1, with token counts)
finding: Gives token counts that earlier lines lacked. Reasoning models use about two orders of magnitude more output tokens than prompted LLMs, and do far better on large-range arithmetic. Raising o3-mini to high effort helped on I-RAVEN but not on the hardest I-RAVEN-X setting.
numbers: Task / arithmetic accuracy / mean output tokens. I-RAVEN range 10: o3-mini medium 86.6 / 74.4 / 5445; o3-mini high 92.6 / 86.1 / 9867; R1 80.6 / 74.8 / 4486; R1-distilled 78.4 / 69.4 / 5192. I-RAVEN-X range 1000: o3-mini medium 81.0 / 60.8 / 7209; high 80.6 / 60.1 / 19449; R1 82.8 / 65.8 / 5505. GPT-4 (7 ICL prompts) at range 1000: 74.0 / 1.1 / 21 tokens; Llama-3 70B (21 prompts) 74.2 / 0.4 / 21. Settings: o3-mini-2025-01-31, 25,000 reasoning-token cap, R1 temperature 0.6.
limits: Symbolic text attributes, no code execution for any model, one run, subset of test items. LLM rows come from the earlier paper, so prompt engineering differs.
agent_relevance: Gives the price of reasoning on this task: about 5,000-19,000 tokens per item against 21 for a prompted GPT-4. Extra effort bought nothing on the hard setting, so a token cap with a verify step is better than more thinking.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) same paper, Table 2 and text (what the 17.0% number really is)
finding: Correction to the headline. The 86.6% to 17.0% drop compares I-RAVEN (3x3, range 10) with I-RAVEN-X (3x10, range 1000, 10 confounders and smoothing pL=0.51). The matched baseline for the 17.0% cell is 81.0%, not 86.6%. Either perturbation alone costs far less; only the combination collapses.
numbers: o3-mini range 1000: clean 81.0%; 10 confounders only 69.8% (13,709 tokens); smoothing pL=0.51 only 75.6% (13,028 tokens); both 17.0% (18,482 tokens). R1: clean 82.8%; confounders 77.0; smoothing pL=0.51 63.0; both 23.2%. High-effort o3-mini on both: 31.0% at 53,596 tokens. Chance 12.5%.
limits: Simulated uncertainty, not a real perception model. No variance reported for the reasoning models.
agent_relevance: The collapse is an interaction: many irrelevant attributes plus uncertain values. Test each stress separately, then together, in any gate.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) I-RAVEN-X, arXiv 2510.17496 (workshop/NeurIPS version), abstract and section 3.2 on superposition
finding: Authors conclude that reasoning models cannot explore several probabilistic outcomes at once. They name two possible causes (longer prompts, or a general limit in probabilistic reasoning) and do not separate them.
numbers: Arithmetic accuracy LLMs 59.3% to 4.4%, LRMs 80.5% to 63.0% across the I-RAVEN to I-RAVEN-X range. Uncertainty costs LRMs 61.8 points of task accuracy.
quote: cannot effectively explore multiple probabilistic outcomes in superposition
limits: Cause not isolated. No arm that keeps explicit parallel hypotheses.
agent_relevance: Gap 7: no LLM test of keeping several rules alive exists in this paper. The supporting evidence comes from the non-LLM model in d06.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2024) Towards learning abductive reasoning using VSA distributed representations (ARLC), Tables 2-4
finding: A rule-learning model that scores every candidate rule with a confidence and combines all rules' predictions by soft selection (a posterior-like mix) is robust across constellations and on unseen rule-attribute pairs. In the uncertainty paper (d04) the entropy-weighted version of this keeps 88.0% where LLMs fall to 17-23%.
numbers: I-RAVEN avg accuracy (10 seeds, trained on 2x2 only): ARLC 92.4-92.6% vs GPT-3 86.5%, NVSA 88.1, PrAE 71.1, Learn-VRF 79.5. Ablation: removing position/number superposition +8.1, context-awareness +2.6, 12-term rule template +2.2 points. OOD unseen rule-attribute pairs: ARLC 98.6-100%, GPT-3 65.8-94.7%.
limits: Trained model, not a prompted LLM. No ablation that switches off the multi-rule soft selection alone, so credit to keeping several rules alive is not isolated. Little et al. 2012 full text was not reachable (abstract only).
agent_relevance: Supports keeping a weighted set of rule hypotheses with confidences, but only by analogy. The LLM-side test is missing, so the schema should treat it as a hypothesis.

source: Haznitrama, Ardi, Oh (2026) NeuroCognition, appendix B.2 and implementation notes (human MC vs Gen pilot, repetitions)
finding: Re-opened. Human text pilot: N=9 adults, each did 15 MC items and 15 Gen items in separate sessions. Means were similar (0.430 MC vs 0.444 Gen), no consistent direction per person, and all preferred MC. RAPM was run once per model, so there is no run-to-run variance for the MC/Gen or reasoning on/off results. Only SWM and WCST had three runs.
numbers: Human text MC 0.430 +/- .167, Gen 0.444 +/- .183 (N=9). Models: GPT-5 MC 0.540 to Gen 0.605; Claude Sonnet 4 0.560 to 0.385; Grok 4 Fast 0.690 to 0.555. Reasoning off: Text MC p=.021 gain; Text Gen p=.83; Image MC p=.173 (4 models able to toggle). RAPM effective thinking budget 30k or 60k tokens; 140 image and 200 text items.
limits: Single run per model on RAPM. Four models in the reasoning toggle. Items are generated string matrices, not shape matrices.
agent_relevance: Gap 9 is NOT closed: no seeds on RAPM. With 200 items the standard error of one accuracy is near 0.035, so some MC-to-Gen swings of 0.05 may be noise.

source: Haznitrama et al. (2026) NeuroCognition, section 5.2 (pattern hints) and Zhang et al. (2019) RAVEN, section 6 (rule loss)
finding: Gap 4 re-read. In RAVEN, adding the rule-set classification loss left WReN unchanged and cut ResNet+DRT from 59.56% to 20.71%; adding a structure loss cut it only to 56.86% (WReN 14.69 to 12.58). The authors give no cause. Barrett's PGM gain (+13.9) was for WReN. Naming rule types to an LLM (NeuroCognition pattern hints, 10 models) had no significant mean effect. The two results are different kinds of thing: one is a training loss on a net, the other a prompt hint.
numbers: RAVEN: loss sum Ltarget + lambda*Lrule. Hints: Text MC p=.177, Text Gen p=.45, Image MC p=.666.
limits: My explanation (original RAVEN answer sets leak, so a rule loss may disturb a shortcut the net had learned) is an inference, not tested by either paper.
agent_relevance: Do not rely on name-the-rule-type prompts. Evidence says the gap is in applying a rule to cells, so verification by execution matters more than rule naming.

source: Green, Bunge, Briones Chiongbian, Barrow, Ferrer (2017) Fluid reasoning predicts future mathematical performance among children and adolescents (J Exp Child Psychol)
finding: Describes the tasks. Analysis-Synthesis: analyse an incomplete logic puzzle of coloured squares and use a key to find the missing colour; calls for general sequential (deductive) reasoning, harder items need more steps. Concept Formation: see instances and non-instances of a concept (for example red square), state the rule; needs inductive reasoning and frequent switching between rules. WASI Matrix Reasoning is the Raven-like induction measure.
numbers: N=69 participants aged 6-21 at three time points (mean age 10.18, 11.67, 13.45). CFA loaded Matrix Reasoning, Analysis-Synthesis and Concept Formation on one Fluid Reasoning factor, all standardised loadings above .65. Tests: WJ-R cognitive subtests.
limits: Small longitudinal sample. Per-test loadings are in a figure not read. WJ-R version, not WJ-IV.
agent_relevance: Maps onto our schema. Concept Formation is rule discovery from positive and negative cases (induction with rival-rule testing). Analysis-Synthesis is executing a key step by step (rule application). Matrix items need both.

source: Dombrowski, McGill, Canivez (2018) Hierarchical exploratory factor analyses of the Woodcock-Johnson IV full test battery (Sch Psychol Q)
finding: In the WJ IV norm data the two subtests load on g about as much as Number Matrices and less than Number Series; the separate Gf factor is not clean (Gf merges with Quantitative at ages 9-13 and does not appear alone at 14-19).
numbers: Norm sample 7,416 (ages 2-90+); school-age matrices average 1,572 (ages 9-13) and 1,685 (14-19). Schmid-Leiman g loading, ages 9-13: Concept Formation .54 (g variance .29, h2 .46), Analysis-Synthesis .50 (.25, h2 .50), Number Matrices .61, Number Series .67. Ages 14-19: Concept Formation .56 (.32, h2 .66), Analysis-Synthesis .52 (.27, h2 .46), Number Matrices .64.
limits: Subtest correlations taken from the Technical Manual, not raw data. WJ IV, not the version in d09. Age-group assignment of the tables inferred from table headings in PDF text.
agent_relevance: Only about 25-30% of each test's variance is g. They are modest g measures, so a score on them is not a stand-in for general reasoning in the gate.

source: Caemmerer, Keith, Reynolds (2020) Beyond individual intelligence tests: application of Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory (Intelligence)
finding: Lists WJ III Analysis-Synthesis and Concept Formation as Gf subtests in a cross-battery sample but gives only descriptive statistics for them.
numbers: Analysis-Synthesis n=87 mean 102.91 SD 17.19; Concept Formation n=89 mean 98.37 SD 16.16.
limits: Descriptives only. No loading for these two tests found in this paper.
agent_relevance: Low. Confirms the Gf label only.

source: Search record, gap 2 (LLM results on Woodcock-Johnson Concept Formation and Analysis-Synthesis)
finding: No LLM or AI evaluation of Woodcock-Johnson Concept Formation or Analysis-Synthesis was found. Only one web search could be spent on it, and it surfaced human factor-analytic papers; the search budget then ran out. Absence is not proof.
limits: Search budget exhausted; Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex and arXiv query APIs returned rate-limit errors.
agent_relevance: Concept Formation resembles Wisconsin Card Sort or ARC-style rule discovery already covered by NeuroCognition WCST. Treat WCST results as the nearest LLM proxy.

source: Beger, Yi, Fu, Denton, Moskvichev, Tsai, Rajamanickam, Mitchell (2026) Distinguishing performance from competence in evaluations of humanlike abstract reasoning (ConceptARC)
finding: Not Raven, but the closest 2025-26 test of reasoning effort plus Python tools on rule-induction grids. Tools help little on text grids and a lot on images. Accuracy overstates concept understanding: about 27% of o3's correct text answers rested on unintended or wrong rules, against about 7% for humans.
numbers: ConceptARC, 480 tasks. o3 text: low 68.3, medium 77.1, low+tools 67.9, medium+tools 75.6. o3 visual: low 6.7, medium 5.6, low+tools 18.1, medium+tools 29.2. Humans 73%. Repeat of 3 runs on 48 tasks: same rule label in all passes for 54.2-56.4% of eligible cases; pairwise rule-label consistency 66.0-70.9%. Temperature 1.0.
limits: Grid tasks, not matrices. Single pass for the main table. Claude and Gemini rows partly garbled in text extraction and not quoted.
agent_relevance: Check the rule the agent states, not only its answer. Run-to-run rule agreement is only about two thirds, so a gate needs repeated runs.

source: Hodel and West (2023/2024) Response: Emergent analogical reasoning in large language models
finding: Replication on letter strings with altered alphabets. GPT-3 held up only on simple problems with the standard English alphabet, while humans stayed high. The authors point to training data. They also cite Mitchell that digit matrices are not equal in difficulty to Raven.
numbers: GPT-3 (text-davinci-003, temperature 0): only 'remove redundant letter' and 'sort' stayed in the original range; comprehension checks reached at least 30% of original level in all but one case.
limits: Letter strings, not matrices, and GPT-3 only. Webb et al. answer with code execution (b02). No test of 2025-26 models.
agent_relevance: Gap 6 stays open for current models on matrices: no follow-up found that runs counterfactual symbols on Raven-style items with reasoning models.

source: Li (2025) A study of rule omission in Raven's Progressive Matrices (arXiv 2510.03127)
finding: Trained transformers and vision nets on I-RAVEN do well on rules seen in training but fall sharply on rules left out of training. High token accuracy hides low whole-answer accuracy.
numbers: Seq-to-seq transformer, same-rule test: 92.62-93.42% average; different-rule test: 47.00% (one rule removed) to 31.47% (two removed). Centre config token accuracy 96.88% but correct-choice accuracy 45.31%. Vision nets under 30% on unseen rules.
limits: Trained from scratch on I-RAVEN, not a pretrained LLM. Single-author preprint.
agent_relevance: Rule-level transfer failure is shown for trained models; for prompted LLMs it is untested. Score whole answers, never partial-token credit.

source: Carpenter, Just, Shell (1990) What one intelligence test measures (Psychological Review 97, 404-431), access attempt
finding: Not read. The APA page loads no text and no open copy was found. Crossref confirms the record (pages 404-431, 1,177 citing works). FAIRAVEN/BETTERAVEN fit, fixation statistics and sample sizes remain unread. Vodegel Matzen error types also unread.
agent_relevance: Gap 5 stays open. Use the Little et al. 2014 figure (57%) with the note that it is second-hand.
